name: Extended virtual addressing
plain: Lets an app use a much larger virtual address space.
meaning: Not about people, but part of the entitlement tier: some capabilities are just a switch in the app.

android.note: 64 bit processes already have a large address space; no switch

ios.note: Enables address space beyond default limits

limits.headline: Can use a larger memory address range on iPhone, but not on Android
limits.user_action: Nothing. The developer turns on a setting before the app ships
can: Map more memory than the default limit on iPhone
Handle very large files or models in heavy apps
Use it with no prompt after Apple approves the setting
cannot: Turn it on from Android; 64 bit apps already have a large range, with no switch
Use more actual memory than the phone has
Gain extra access to your data
limits.differs: This setting exists only on iPhone. On Android it is not needed.

story.what_it_is: A switch that lets a big app use much more memory address space.

marketing.name: Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement
marketing.pitch: Developer rule: apps with large memory needs can ask for a bigger virtual address space.

story.for_you: You will never see it. It simply helps big apps like large games, video editors or maps load huge files without crashing.
story.for_makers: It is a technical switch in the app's settings. Makers turn it on when their app maps big files or large worlds into memory. It does not collect any data about you.

use_cases.example: An open world game maps a huge world file into memory so it can stream it smoothly.
A video editor opens a very large project without running out of address space.
A map app loads a large offline map file as one piece.
An AR scene app holds big 3D scans in memory while you scan a room.
A developer who gets random memory errors tries this switch first.

story.ios_note: Needs an Apple entitlement, with no prompt to you.
